## 1. Overview – “Hi‑Tech Voice, Hi‑Polite” | Goal | What we aim to achieve in 2026 | |------|--------------------------------| | **Core Product Vision** | An *intelligent*, *always‑listening* assistant that feels “polite” and “trusted” in every culture you serve. | | **Key Success Drivers** | 1. **Interaction Style**: honorific tone, user‑controlled command culture, proactive‑but‑respectful flow.
2. **Household Roles**: family‑centric use‑cases, inter‑generational data sharing, context‑aware family management.
3. **Privacy Signaling** | Transparent, localized cues that the device is recording/processing, with user‑controlled “silent” modes aligned to local comfort with always‑present listening devices. | | **Outcome Metrics** | • Adoption (DAU per household)
• “Politeness‑Score” from in‑app feedback
• Privacy‑Confidence rating
• Family‑Share‑Ratio
• Compliance audit score 95 %+ | --- ## 2. Interaction Style (Honorifics & Command Comfort) | Region | Honorific System | Key Language Features | User‑Command Comfort | Design Implications | |--------|------------------|-----------------------|----------------------|---------------------| | **Japan** | Two‑tier honorific: *尊敬語（そんけいご）* (respectful) & *謙譲語（けんじょうご）* (humble). Context‑based switching. | Use “–desu–masu” polite forms, honorific titles (*san*, *sama*). Soft “koto” or “nan desu ka?” endings. | Low – users prefer polite requests, rarely shout. | **Model**: Dual‑tone policy – app‑level “polite” default; “command mode” toggled with “Hey [AI], start command mode.”
**UI**: Haptic “tick‑tock” when waiting for command. | | **Korea** | Three‑tier system: *존댓말 (jondaetmal)* (honorific), *반말 (banmal)* (informal), *말투 (mal-tu)* (speech style). | 80–90 % of home conversations are 존댓말; switching often at family boundaries. | Moderate – older generation uses polite, teens use banmal. | **Model**: Voice‑level user profile (age, gender) auto‑detects politeness level; UI offers “Switch to Banmal” button.
**UI**: “Korean‑style” soft‑tone waveform display. | | **Thailand** | Three registers: *คำสั่ง (Kham‑Sang)* (command), *ขอร้อง (Khor‑Rang)* (request), *คำถาม (Kham‑Tham)* (question). Tone influences meaning. | High – customers enjoy “telling” devices; “ขอคุณ” (please‑you). | High – loud commanding is common, especially with children or in cafés. | **Model**: Default “คำสั่ง” mode. Provide “Polite Request” context by detecting “ขอ” prefix.
**UI**: Color cues (soft blue for polite, orange for command). | | **Gulf (KSA / UAE)** | Arabic has *Ḥaṣn (honorific)* vs *Tartīf (casual)*; strong use of *sir* / *madam* titles. | Low – formal voice commands, especially for men, women use polite forms. | Low – “commanding” is limited; commands usually phrased politely. | **Model**: AI default to *Ḥaṣn* style with *sir* for men, *madam* for women; optional “Casual” toggle.
**UI**: Arabic calligraphy stylized voice wave. | ### 2.1 Interaction Flow Blueprint 1. **Boot‑up Greeting** - *Japan/Korea*: “おはようございます、[Name]さん。” / “안녕하세요, [Name]님.” - *Thailand*: “สวัสดีครับ/ค่ะ [Name].” - *Gulf*: “[Name]님 안녕하세요. (English)” 2. **Command‑Mode Toggle** - Default: “polite‑mode” listening for request. - **User**: “Hey Assistant, start command mode.” - AI switches to high‑volume, low‑politeness “command” voice. 3. **Respectful Confirmation** - AI repeats action in honorific tone: “了解いたしました。” / “알겠습니다.” - Visual cue: soft fade‑in of “🕰️” icon. 4. **If user interrupts** - AI politely pauses: “失礼しました。” / “죄송합니다.” - Resumes once signal “go ahead” received. 5. **Easter‑Eggs for Cultural Pride** - *Japan*: “お茶を入れましょうか？” - *Korea*: “한강에 가볼래요?” - *Thailand*: “ยามเย็นพร้อมเสิร์ฟชา?”. --- ## 3. Household Roles & Family Management | Region | Typical Household Structure | Family‑Related Features | Implementation Notes | |--------|----------------------------|------------------------|----------------------| | **Japan** | Multi‑generational (grandparents + nuclear) | • “祖父母専用コモンボックス” – separate “family‑timeline” for elders. • Family “Respect Table”: each member’s politeness level auto‑recorded. | Data stored in separate "Family Segment" with stricter consent rules. | | **Korea** | Multi‑generational, but younger adults often live in separate homes (student, workers). | • “장인 도구” – senior‑friendly voice commands (“집에 가니까 알파벳”). • “채널” – each generation distinct “profile”. | Voice‑profile can be switched by voice (“스르르 전환”). | | **Thailand** | Extended families in one dwelling; many children/young adults. | • “Family Chat” – group chat for family announcements; children “voice stickers”. • “Senior Safe‑Mode” auto‑activates if elder not heard after 5 min. | Visual family tree on home screen. | | **Gulf** | Large households, multi‑familial units (e.g., tenants, relatives). | • “Unit Access” – voice‑controlled door locks with honorific address (“Sir”). • “Family Group” – hierarchical scheduling (father > mother > children). | Integrate local HME (Home Management Engine) standard. | ### 3.1 Voice‑Controlled Family Scheduler | Feature | How it works | Privacy Controls | |---------|--------------|------------------| | **Family Calendar** | Voice command adds events, tags by family role. | “Family‑only” vs “Everyone‑only” visibility toggles. | | **Meal Planner** | AI suggests menus respecting dietary restrictions and honorific titles for elders. | Users can “block” certain ingredients/people from access. | | **Care Alerts** | Voice‑alerts for med‑reminder, fall detection (Sensus). | “Silent” mode when elder is present. | | **Mood‑Heatmap** | Aggregated mood trend across family. | Anonymized; elder has “view‑only.” | ### 3.2 Multi‑User Identification - **Voice‑print**: Each member registers voice biometric profile with a consent dialog. - **Family Card**: NFC badge for each household member to authenticate voice‑less interactions. - **Role‑Based Defaults**: Elder’s home settings auto‑apply at night; child‑friendly voice “Cheerful”. --- ## 4. Privacy Signaling & Trust | Region | Local Privacy Expectation | Physical Signal | Haptic/Haptic‑Audio Cue | Auditory Feedback Loops | |--------|---------------------------|-----------------|--------------------------|--------------------------| | **Japan** | Highly sensitive, “shame” around being recorded. | Small “赤いシール” (red sticker) that appears on the front. | 1 Hz vibration before recording. | “おやすみ” で “録音中” “録音停止”. | | **Korea** | Growing awareness, value personal data. | Light “LED ring” changes from green (idle) to red (recording). | 2 Hz vibration + beep. | “지금은 기록 중임” announcement. | | **Thailand** | Privacy norms vary; older individuals cautious. | “ข้าวกระป๋ง” style “safe‑zone” icon on screen. | 3 Hz gentle vibration. | “บันทึกเสียงทำงาน” (recording) & “หยุดบันทึก” (stop). | | **Gulf** | Very cautious; “data sovereignty” key. | “KSA flag” visible ring on top. | 1–2 Hz pulsing. | “يتم تسجيل” (recording) & “السوابق متوقف” (stop). | ### 4.1 Design Tactics - **Always‑On Mic Visibility**: Small, translucent "mic" icon that lights up when listening. - **Privacy “Badge”**: Device shows real‑time recording status on its face. - **“Do‑Not‑Disturb”**: Voice command (“Stop & pause”) activates silent mode. - **Data‑Storage Dashboard**: User can view what data is kept (audio logs, usage). ### 4.2 Compliance & Certification - **Japan**: P2C, APPI, local privacy audit. - **Korea**: PIPA, Korean Telecom Regulatory Authority. - **Thailand**: PDPA, local data residency. - **Gulf**: UAE “Digital Trust Seal”, Saudi Vision, local cyber‑law compliance. --- ## 5. Feature Prioritization by Region | Feature | Japan | Korea | Thailand | Gulf | |--------|-------|-------|----------|------| | **AI Voice‑Response Politeness** | ✅ 1st priority – core. | ✅ 1st priority – core. | ✅ 1st priority – core. | ✅ 1st priority – core. | | **Multi‑User Voice Recognition** | ✅ 2nd priority. | ✅ 2nd priority. | ✅ 2nd priority. | ✅ 2nd priority. | | **Family “Respect” Scheduler** | ✅ 3rd priority. | ✅ 3rd priority. | ✅ 3rd priority. | ✅ 3rd priority. | | **Dynamic “Command Mode” Override** | ✅ 4th priority. | ✅ 4th priority. | ✅ 4th priority. | ✅ 4th priority. | | **Localized Smart‑Home Integration** | ✅ 5th priority. | ✅ 5th priority. | ✅ 5th priority. | ✅ 5th priority. | | **“Silent” Family‑Safe Mode** | ✅ 6th priority. | ✅ 6th priority. | ✅ 6th priority. | ✅ 6th priority. | | **Voice‑Based Payment** (WeChat Pay / Alipay / Alipay‑KR / Islamic‑Friendly Mobile Wallets) | ✅ 7th priority (post‑MVP). | ✅ 7th priority (post‑MVP). | ✅ 7th priority (post‑MVP). | ✅ 7th priority (post‑MVP). | ### 5.1 Roadmap Slice | Quarter | Japan | Korea | Thailand | Gulf | |---------|-------|-------|----------|------| | Q1 2026 | MVP with polite‑voice + data‑privacy badges. | MVP w/ honorific AI + voice‑print. | MVP with family group & “silent” mode. | MVP with “sir/madam” honorifics + data‑silo. | | Q2 2026 | Family Scheduler pilot. | Household Profile engine. | “Voice‑Sticker” emoji integration. | “Family‑Unit” access control pilot. | | Q3 2026 | Cross‑device UI sync. | Multi‑Device sync + HME integration. | Integration with local e‑payment. | Mobile wallet & smart‑home lock. | | Q4 2026 | Full global rollout + market‑specific updates. | Full rollout + local legal certifications. | Full rollout + community events. | Full rollout + AI‑driven health recommendations. | --- ## 6. Risk & Mitigation | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | |------|------------|--------|------------| | **Cultural Rejection** | Medium | High | Pre‑launch anthropological field‑tests; local ambassadors; iterative A/B testing. | | **Regulatory Gap** | Low | Very High | Hire local compliance specialists; continuous update of privacy rules. | | **Privacy Breach** | Low | High | Mandatory end‑to‑end encryption; zero‑knowledge audit; user‑controlled data deletion. | | **Mis‑interpretation of Honorific Levels** | High | Medium | Continuous ML tuning; user feedback loop for tone adjustment. | | **Family Conflict over Data Sharing** | Medium | Medium | Transparent opt‑in/out UI; separate "Family‑Priv" & "Personal‑Priv" data stores. | --- ## 7. Design Deliverables for Stakeholders | Deliverable | Content | Who Owns | |-------------|---------|----------| | **Voice Tone Library** | Samples of 3 politesse levels per language. | Localization Team | | **Family‑Role UI Kit** | Icons for elder, child, adult, shared. | UI/UX Lead | | **Privacy‑Signal Prototype** | Visual + haptic + audio cues mockup. | Product Ops | | **Compliance Checklist** | GDPR, APPI, PDPA, Saudi Data Law. | Legal & Compliance | | **Feature Roadmap** | Phase‑by‑phase rollout timeline. | Executive Product | | **Localized KPI Dashboard** | Adoption, Politeness‑Score, Privacy‑Confidence. | Data Analytics | --- ## 8. Quick‑Start Playbook (First 90 Days) 1. **User Study (Weeks 1–4)** – Recruit 40 families per region, collect usage data. 2. **Politeness Model Training (Weeks 5–8)** – Fine‑tune TTS/ASR for honorific levels. 3. **Privacy‑Signal A/B (Week 9)** – Test two signal designs, measure user preference. 4. **Family‑Scheduler MVP (Week 10–12)** – Launch pilot, gather feedback, iterate. 5. **Compliance Checks (Week 12)** – Final audit before regional launch. --- ### Bottom Line By treating **“politeness”** and **“family context”** as first‑class features, and by making **privacy signaling** culturally resonant, the voice assistant will not only meet local expectations but become a *trusted family companion* rather than a foreign intruder. The prioritization matrix ensures we deliver the high‑impact features fast while laying a compliant, privacy‑centric foundation for scalable growth across Japan, Korea, Thailand, and the Gulf.
